messages.text: Me and my wife have three kids. I get paid every two weeks. Do we qualify for SNAP or TennCare?

Thanks for telling me about your family. I need a few details to check this properly.

1. How old are your three kids, and is anyone in the family pregnant or has a disability?
2. How much do you get paid every two weeks **before taxes**? Does your wife have any income too?

I'm not sure where the kids' ages come in, but here's what I can tell you. Kids are 10, 6 and 3. Wait, I said five of us, my wife and me plus the three kids. Nobody's pregnant and nobody has a disability.

I get paid $1,600 every two weeks before taxes. My wife doesn't have any income, she stays home.

Your family looks like it could get help from a few programs. Only the agency can decide, and everything below is a first look.

**Your income:** $1,600 every two weeks is about **$3,467 a month** before taxes. I got that by multiplying by 26 paychecks and dividing by 12.

## TennCare for your kids: likely
Tennessee's chart for a household of 5 shows these monthly limits:
- Ages 1–5 (your 3-year-old): $4,578
- Ages 6–18 (your 6- and 10-year-olds): $4,288
- Your income of about $3,467 is under both limits.

CoverKids is a backup for children under 19. Its limit for a family of 5 is $8,059 a month.

Source: [TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/tenncare/members-applicants/eligibility-reference-guide.html). That page doesn't show a date for the chart, so the agency will use its current numbers.

## TennCare for you and your wife: unlikely
The limit for parents is $3,224 a month for a family of 5. Your income is a bit above that. You can still apply, because the agency may count your income differently than I did.

## Food assistance (SNAP): possibly, and worth applying
- **Income test:** Your income looks under the usual limit. I found limits of about $4,079 to $4,191 a month for 5 people. Those came from third-party sites, not an official page.
- **Unsettled rule:** Tennessee's income limit is unsettled. It may be 130% of poverty, or it may be 200%. Either way, you look under the limit, so please apply.
- **Deductions:** SNAP subtracts part of your pay and some costs, like rent, utilities and child care. I couldn't open an official page with the current deduction amounts, so I can't give a dollar estimate yet.
- **Savings:** SNAP may have a limit on savings. Sources disagree on the amount (about $2,750 to $3,000), so the caseworker will tell you.

## WIC: possibly, for your 3-year-old
WIC helps kids under 5. The limit is 185% of poverty, and your income looks well under that. A WIC clinic does a short health check too. I couldn't open Tennessee's current WIC table, so confirm the dollar limit with the clinic.

## How to apply
- **Food assistance (SNAP):** [One DHS portal](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp) or call 1-833-772-8347 (TTY 711). Source: [Tennessee Department of Human Services](https://www.tn.gov/humanservices/for-families/supplemental-nutrition-assistance-program-snap.html).
- **TennCare and CoverKids:** [tn.gov/tenncare](https://www.tn.gov/tenncare). I didn't open a page with the phone number, so call 211 for it.
- **WIC:** Call your county health department, or call 211.
- **Free local help:** Call **211**.

Reporting your income accurately protects you. If a benefit is paid out by mistake, you may have to pay it back.

To get you a SNAP estimate, I need two things:
1. How much is your rent or mortgage each month?
2. Do you pay for heating or cooling separately? Do you pay for child care so you can work?
Rent is $1,200 a month. Yes, we pay heating and cooling separately. No child care costs.

Based on these numbers, you will **likely** get food assistance (SNAP). My rough estimate is **at least $465 a month**, and probably more. That is an estimate, and only the agency decides.

## Why it looks likely
I used the new SNAP numbers that started October 1, 2026, for a family of 5.

| Step | Amount |
|---|---|
| Your income before taxes | about $3,467 a month |
| Limit on income before deductions (130% of poverty) | $4,191, and you're under it |
| Take off 20% of pay | −$693, which leaves about $2,773 |
| Take off the standard deduction | −$268, which leaves about $2,505 |
| Limit after deductions (100% of poverty) | $3,224, and you're under it |

You pass both income tests. This holds whether Tennessee's limit turns out to be 130% or 200% of poverty.

## The estimate
SNAP gives families up to **$1,217 a month** for 5 people. That amount shrinks by 30 cents for every dollar of income left after deductions.

- **Rent alone:** Your $1,200 rent doesn't lower your income further. SNAP only counts rent above half of your remaining income, and half of $2,505 is about $1,253. That gives about **$465 a month**.
- **Rent plus heating and cooling:** Because you pay heating and cooling separately, SNAP adds a set utility amount to your rent. That likely pushes your costs over the line and raises your benefit. I couldn't find Tennessee's utility amount, so I can't give a firm number. As an example, a $400 utility amount would put your estimate near **$580**.
- The most a family can get is capped by a limit on the rent deduction (up to $769), so the estimate shouldn't go far above about $700.

The caseworker will use your real bills and the exact amounts.

## Sources
- [FY2027 SNAP figures](https://benefitguide.net/guides/snap-changes-october-1-2026/). This is a summary site, not an official page. USDA's own FY2027 memo wouldn't open for me, so these figures may be off by a dollar or two.
- [Tennessee Department of Human Services, SNAP](https://www.tn.gov/humanservices/for-families/supplemental-nutrition-assistance-program-snap.html)
- [TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/tenncare/members-applicants/eligibility-reference-guide.html)

## Notes
- There may be a limit on savings (sources say about $2,750 to $3,000). Do you want me to check this? Just tell me roughly how much you have in savings.
- Don't wait on the savings question. You can still apply, and the caseworker will check it.

## Next steps
- **SNAP:** Apply at [onedhs.tn.gov/csp](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp) or call 1-833-772-8347 (TTY 711). Have ready: proof of ID, income (pay stubs), rent and utility bills.
- **TennCare or CoverKids for the kids:** Apply at [tn.gov/tenncare](https://www.tn.gov/tenncare).
- **WIC for your 3-year-old:** Call your county health department.
- **Free local help with any of these:** Call **211**.

Report your income and household accurately on every application. If a benefit is paid out by mistake, you may have to pay it back.

Links: [{"title":"snap benefits increase for millions of americans","url":"https://www.news4jax.com/news/local/2026/10/02/snap-benefits-increase-for-millions-of-americans/"},{"title":"Appendix B - Table of Standards","url":"https://www.nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/SNAP/Content/History/Appendix%20B%20Table%20of%20Standards/Appendix B - Table of Standards October.1.2025 - March.31.2026.htm"},{"title":"Appendix B - Table of Standards","url":"https://www.nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/SNAP/Content/Appendix B - Table of Standards.htm"},{"title":"Back to Blog","url":"https://benefitsusa.org/en/blog/snap-income-limits-2027-projected-chart"},{"title":"www.srca.nm.gov","url":"https://www.srca.nm.gov/nmac/nmregister/xxix/8.139.500amend.pdf"},{"title":"Appendix B - Table of Standards","url":"https://www.nd.gov/dhs/policymanuals/SNAP/Content/History/Appendix%20B%20Table%20of%20Standards/Appendix B - Table of Standards.htm"},{"title":"Back to Blog","url":"https://benefitsusa.org/en/blog/snap-income-limits-2027-projections"},{"title":"SNAP Income Limits FY2027 Confirmed: Single Applicants Capped at $1,729, Family of Four at $3,575","url":"https://govtschemes.org/?p=38175"},{"title":"www.otda.ny.gov","url":"https://www.otda.ny.gov/programs/publications/5104.pdf"}]

The search turned up a figure of about $4,191 per month in gross income for a five-person household in FY2027, but the sources disagree on whether it is official yet.

- **Official or projected?** One site labels its FY2027 numbers "confirmed" and says they take effect October 1, 2026, and its table includes the five-person figure, $4,191 (effective October 1, 2026; FY2027 limit for 5 people shown as $4,191). Another site calls its 2027 numbers projections and says final figures may differ by a dollar or two per household size once USDA publishes its official FY2027 cost-of-living adjustment memo. I could not find the USDA memo itself, so treat $4,191 as likely but unverified.
- **Current baseline (FY2026):** The five-person gross limit at 130% of poverty is $4,079 per month, according to North Dakota's policy manual (Gross Monthly Income Standards, 130% of Poverty Level, household size 5).
- **Cross-check:** A news report on the FY2027 changes gives the four-person and single-person limits, $3,575 and $1,729, which match the projected table (48 states, D.C., Guam, and the U.S. Virgin Islands).
- **Context:** The gross test is a federal floor. Many states use broad-based categorical eligibility, and many states set their BBCE threshold at 200% of the federal poverty line, so state rules can differ. The net income test, set at 100% of poverty, still applies in most cases.

For the authoritative figure, check the USDA FNS cost-of-living adjustment memo for FY2027.

Links: [{"title":"Tn Food Stamp Income Limit","url":"https://congresoextension.utn.edu.ar/tn-food-stamp-income-limit"},{"title":"Policy%2024.18%20SNAP%20Deductions%20from%20Income Esigned","url":"https://TN.gov/content/dam/tn/human-services/documents/Policy%2024.18%20SNAP%20Deductions%20from%20Income_Esigned.pdf"},{"title":"Comprehensive Guide To The SNAP Application TN: Securing Your Food Assistance Benefits","url":"https://leads.easy-sales.com/tn-securing-your-food-assistance-t9an.html"},{"title":"tennessee snap eligibility 2026","url":"https://benefitsusa.org/en/blog/tennessee-snap-eligibility-2026"},{"title":"Administrative and Government Law","url":"https://legalclarity.org/tn-food-stamp-eligibility-calculator-and-income-limits/"},{"title":"Navigating Food Stamps in Tennessee: A Comprehensive Guide to SNAP Benefits","url":"https://001.arktimes.com/?p=20789"},{"title":"Administrative and Government Law","url":"https://legalclarity.org/tennessee-food-stamps-eligibility-benefits-and-rules/"},{"title":"Table I: SNAP Deductions SR 19-09, 09/19 (FSM-A) |","url":"https://dhhs.nh.gov/fsmar_htm/html/601_table_i_snap_deductions_sr_19-09_09_19_fsm_a.htm"},{"title":"snapeligibilitycalculator.com","url":"https://snapeligibilitycalculator.com/?p=4170"}]

The search turned up useful detail, but the sources disagree on several figures, and the one official Tennessee document is from 2018.

- **Income tests:** Most households must pass a gross income test at 130% of the federal poverty level and a net income test at 100% (gross income before deductions can't exceed 130 percent of the poverty level, and net income after allowable deductions can't exceed 100 percent). Households with an elderly or disabled member only need to meet the net test (per TDHS eligibility information).
- **Gross limits conflict:** One guide lists a one-person gross limit of $1,729 per month for October 2025 through September 2026 (BenefitsUSA). Another gives $1,696 for one person and $3,483 for a family of four for FY2026 (legalclarity.org, citing Food and Nutrition Service figures).
- **Deductions:** The standard deduction is listed at $209 per month for households of 1–3, $223 for four, $261 for five, and $299 for six or more (snapeligibilitycalculator.com). The excess shelter deduction is listed as shelter costs over half of net income, capped at $744 (same source). Other sources describe the shelter deduction in the same general way, without the cap figure (congresoextension.utn.edu.ar). Deductions also include a share of earned income, dependent care, child support, and, for elderly or disabled members, unreimbursed medical costs above $35 per month (legalclarity.org).
- **Asset limits conflict:** One source gives $2,750 in countable resources, or $4,250 for households with someone 60 or older or disabled (legalclarity.org). Another gives $3,000 and $4,500 (snapeligibilitycalculator.com).
- **Official source:** TDHS Policy 24.18 on SNAP deductions from income is dated August 2018 and says TDHS meets federal and state guidelines on deductions. Its specific dollar amounts are likely outdated.

Bottom line: the 130% and 100% FPL structure is consistent across sources, but the exact dollar figures, particularly the standard deduction, shelter cap, and asset limits, differ. Verify current amounts against the TDHS SNAP pages or the USDA Food and Nutrition Service FY2026 standards before relying on them.

The most consistent answer across the results is that CoverKids covers children under 19 in households at or below 250% of the federal poverty level for 2026.

- **Official state chart:** The TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide lists CoverKids at 250% of the poverty level, for children under 19 who don't qualify for another TennCare category. CoverKids is available to children under age 19 and the unborn children of women who are not eligible under another TennCare category. At or below 250% of the poverty level.
- **2026 dollar figures:** One guide puts 250% of FPL at $39,900 for a single-person household and $82,500 for a family of four. A second source gives the same $82,500 figure for a family of four.
- **Discrepancy on the percentage:** Talk to MIRA says its limits include the 5% income disregard, so they run 5 points above the percentages Tennessee prints on its own chart. So the 250% figure may be the state's printed number, while some outlets report a slightly higher effective threshold. It's worth confirming on the official chart.
- **Dated sources:** Some pages still use 2025 poverty guidelines. One says the official 2026 FPL adjustments are expected in late January 2026 and will likely increase these limits slightly. Use the official TennCare chart for final numbers.
- **Other figures conflict:** Sources disagree on the TennCare Medicaid child thresholds (for example, 138% for ages 6–18 in one source and 133% in another) and on the pregnancy limit (195%, 200%, or 250%). These don't affect the CoverKids limit itself, but they matter if you're comparing programs.

Based on these numbers, you will **likely** get food assistance (SNAP). My rough estimate is **at least $465 a month**, and probably more. That is an estimate, and only the agency decides.

## Why it looks likely
I used the new SNAP numbers that started October 1, 2026, for a family of 5.

| Step | Amount |
|---|---|
| Your income before taxes | about $3,467 a month |
| Limit on income before deductions (130% of poverty) | $4,191, and you're under it |
| Take off 20% of pay | −$693, which leaves about $2,773 |
| Take off the standard deduction | −$268, which leaves about $2,505 |
| Limit after deductions (100% of poverty) | $3,224, and you're under it |

You pass both income tests. This holds whether Tennessee's limit turns out to be 130% or 200% of poverty.

## The estimate
SNAP gives families up to **$1,217 a month** for 5 people. That amount shrinks by 30 cents for every dollar of income left after deductions.

- **Rent alone:** Your $1,200 rent doesn't lower your income further. SNAP only counts rent above half of your remaining income, and half of $2,505 is about $1,253. That gives about **$465 a month**.
- **Rent plus heating and cooling:** Because you pay heating and cooling separately, SNAP adds a set utility amount to your rent. That likely pushes your costs over the line and raises your benefit. I couldn't find Tennessee's utility amount, so I can't give a firm number. As an example, a $400 utility amount would put your estimate near **$580**.
- The most a family can get is capped by a limit on the rent deduction (up to $769), so the estimate shouldn't go far above about $700.

The caseworker will use your real bills and the exact amounts.

## Sources
- [FY2027 SNAP figures](https://benefitguide.net/guides/snap-changes-october-1-2026/). This is a summary site, not an official page. USDA's own FY2027 memo wouldn't open for me, so these figures may be off by a dollar or two.
- [Tennessee Department of Human Services, SNAP](https://www.tn.gov/humanservices/for-families/supplemental-nutrition-assistance-program-snap.html)
- [TennCare Eligibility Reference Guide](https://www.tn.gov/tenncare/members-applicants/eligibility-reference-guide.html)

## Notes
- There may be a limit on savings (sources say about $2,750 to $3,000). Do you want me to check this? Just tell me roughly how much you have in savings.
- Don't wait on the savings question. You can still apply, and the caseworker will check it.

## Next steps
- **SNAP:** Apply at [onedhs.tn.gov/csp](https://onedhs.tn.gov/csp) or call 1-833-772-8347 (TTY 711). Have ready: proof of ID, income (pay stubs), rent and utility bills.
- **TennCare or CoverKids for the kids:** Apply at [tn.gov/tenncare](https://www.tn.gov/tenncare).
- **WIC for your 3-year-old:** Call your county health department.
- **Free local help with any of these:** Call **211**.

Report your income and household accurately on every application. If a benefit is paid out by mistake, you may have to pay it back.
